questions.q: What is the structure of the general solution to a linear nonhomogeneous equation $L[y] = g(x)$?
choices: $y(x) = y_c(x) + y_p(x)$, where $y_c$ is the complementary solution and $y_p$ is any particular solution
questions.answer: By linearity, the general solution of a nonhomogeneous linear equation is the sum of the complementary solution $y_c$ to the homogeneous equation and any particular solution $y_p$.
Try constant $y_p = A$. Then $y_p' = 0, y_p'' = 0$. Substituting: $6A = 12 \Rightarrow A = 2$.

questions.q: What is the trial particular solution $y_p$ for $y'' + 4y = 3x^2 - 1$?
questions.answer: For a quadratic polynomial forcing term $g(x) = 3x^2 - 1$, the standard trial solution is a complete quadratic polynomial $y_p = A x^2 + B x + C$.

questions.q: Find a particular solution to $y'' + y = 4e^{2x}$.
questions.answer: Try $y_p = A e^{2x}$. $y_p'' = 4A e^{2x}$. Substitute: $4A e^{2x} + A e^{2x} = 5A e^{2x} = 4e^{2x} \Rightarrow 5A = 4 \Rightarrow A = 4/5$.

questions.q: What is the correct undetermined coefficients form for $y'' + 9y = 5\cos(2x)$?
questions.answer: Because $\cos(2x)$ produces both sines and cosines upon differentiation, the complete form is $A\cos(2x) + B\sin(2x)$.

questions.q: When must a trial particular solution $y_p$ be multiplied by $x$ (or $x^2$)?
choices: When any term in the trial solution is already a solution of the associated homogeneous equation
Whenever the forcing function is a polynomial
When the coefficient of $y'$ is negative
Only when the right-hand side is zero
questions.answer: If a term in the proposed $y_p$ is part of the complementary solution $y_c$, substituting it will yield zero; multiplying by $x$ restores linear independence.

questions.q: For $y'' - 4y' + 4y = 3e^{2x}$, the homogeneous solution is $y_c = (c_1 + c_2 x)e^{2x}$. What is the correct trial form for $y_p$?
questions.answer: Both $e^{2x}$ and $x e^{2x}$ are in $y_c$. Multiplying by $x^2$ produces $y_p = A x^2 e^{2x}$, which is linearly independent of $y_c$.

questions.q: What physical phenomenon occurs when an undamped mechanical system is driven at its natural resonance frequency ($y'' + \omega_0^2 y = F_0 \cos(\omega_0 t)$)?
choices: Resonance, where amplitude grows linearly with time ($y_p = C t \sin(\omega_0 t)$)
questions.answer: Because the forcing frequency equals the natural frequency, the particular solution takes the form $t\sin(\omega_0 t)$, producing unbounded linearly growing oscillations (resonance).

questions.q: If $y_{p1}$ solves $L[y] = g_1(x)$ and $y_{p2}$ solves $L[y] = g_2(x)$, what solves $L[y] = 2g_1(x) - 3g_2(x)$?
questions.answer: By the linearity of differential operators, $L[2y_{p1} - 3y_{p2}] = 2L[y_{p1}] - 3L[y_{p2}] = 2g_1(x) - 3g_2(x)$.

questions.q: Can the Method of Undetermined Coefficients be used to solve $y'' + y = \tan x$?
choices: No, because derivatives of $\tan x$ produce infinitely many non-terminating forms; Variation of Parameters is required
Yes, with trial solution $A\tan x + B\sec x$
Yes, with trial solution $A\sin x / \cos x$
questions.answer: Undetermined coefficients applies only to functions with finite dimensional spaces of derivatives (polynomials, exponentials, sines/cosines). For $\tan x$, variation of parameters must be used.
Let $y_p = Ax + B$. $y_p'' = 0$. $4(Ax + B) = 4Ax + 4B = 8x + 12 \Rightarrow 4A = 8 \Rightarrow A = 2$ and $4B = 12 \Rightarrow B = 3$. Thus $y_p = 2x + 3$.
